meanings.note: Contrast. Core Russian conj meaning 'and, but; so' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Drawing attention.

examples.trans: I can see the toy car.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: predicative: очень вкусно = it's delicious
Вкусно готовить = to cook well.
For emphasis.

examples.trans: I have no idea at all.

examples.text: Я человек чистый. Я вообще не вор.
examples.trans: I'm an honest man. I'm not a thief at all.

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
Disbelief.
+ dative of person + accusative of thing
+ infinitive: не даёт мне готовить
imperative давай/давайте + 1st person plural or infinitive

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

related.gloss: to hand in; to take (an exam)

meanings.note: adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

зато.gloss: but on the other hand, to make up for it

meanings.en: but on the other hand, at least
meanings.note: introduces a compensating positive fact

examples.text: Четыре по алгебре, зато по физкультуре пятёрка.
examples.trans: A four in algebra, but a five in gym.
The flat is small, but at least it's in the centre.

examples.text: Ничего страшного. Сейчас зато аппетит нагуляем.
examples.trans: No big deal. At least we'll walk up an appetite now.

meanings.note: Asks about the purpose.

examples.trans: Oh, Samson. What have you come for?

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Question word. Core Russian adv meaning 'how; as' in everyday speech.
Как вы знаете = as you know. Core Russian adv meaning 'how; as' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

examples.text: Кто опять трогал мою любимую кастрюлю?!
examples.trans: Who touched my favorite pot again?!

meanings.note: Agrees with the thing owned. Core Russian det meaning 'my, mine' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary
meanings.note: Надо + infinitive.

examples.trans: We need to do even more.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
usually in the genitive ничего, with не: ничего не осталось

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('new').

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to her', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Она нашла нас на новом месте.
examples.trans: She found us at the new place.
That is it, she got really offended.
She is not answering her phone.

meanings.note: Core Russian pron meaning 'they' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.

meanings.note: 'здесь плохо пахнет' = it smells bad here

examples.text: Послушайте, а можно в другое место? Здесь плохо пахнет.
examples.trans: Listen, could we go somewhere else? It smells bad in here.

examples.text: А вы мне тоже айфон подарите?
examples.trans: Will you give me an iPhone too?

поесть.gloss: to eat, to have a meal

meanings.en: to eat, to have something to eat
meanings.note: Perfective of есть. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'есть').

examples.text: Ну ладно, брось! Мы только поедим.
examples.trans: Oh come on, stop it! We'll only eat.

пользоваться.gloss: to use, to take advantage of

meanings.en: to use, to make use of
meanings.note: + instrumental.
+ instrumental: пользоваться слабостью

examples.trans: You're taking advantage of my weakness!
Of course I am. It's blackmail.

meanings.en: to make up, to make peace
meanings.note: Помириться с кем + instrumental. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'мириться').

examples.text: Когда-нибудь ты захочешь помириться со своим папой.
examples.trans: Someday you will want to make up with your dad.

examples.text: Я сто раз хотела с ним помириться!
examples.trans: I wanted to make up with him a hundred times!

examples.text: Хорошо, я согласна помириться с тобой.
examples.trans: Good, I agree to make peace with you.

meanings.note: Поставить защёлку = fit a latch. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'ставить').
Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'ставить').

examples.trans: Put your foot on the bed.

examples.text: Заходите. Поставьте, пожалуйста, правую ногу на кровать.
examples.trans: Come in. Please put your right foot on the bed.

meanings.note: Prefix 'рас-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'слабиться').

examples.text: Ваня, расслабься. В этот раз без обмана.
examples.trans: Vanya, relax. This time there's no trick.

meanings.note: Adverb.
Рядом с + instrumental.

examples.trans: Right nearby, round the corner, there's a cheburek café.

examples.text: Теперь меня рядом с ним похоронить не хотят!
examples.trans: Now they won't even bury me next to him!

examples.text: Тут рядом, за углом, чебуречная. Там нормально.
examples.trans: Right nearby, round the corner, there's a cheburek café. It's fine there.

meanings.en: to sit down, to take a seat

examples.trans: He sat down on a chair.
Listen, sit down. Sit down, please.

meanings.note: Intentionally.
For a particular purpose.

examples.trans: Are you doing this on purpose?
Are you doing this on purpose or what?
You left it here on purpose.

meanings.note: To someone you call ты. Core Russian det meaning 'your (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.note: One person, informal. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

увидеться.gloss: to see each other, meet up

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'видеться').

examples.text: Послушай, мы сегодня увидимся вечером с тобой?
examples.trans: Listen, will we see each other this evening?
All right, see you in the kitchen, administrator!

points at something: это моё = that's mine

meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.
